clue.text: Medal fixed into clothing for high achievement

indicators.note: the medal is fixed into the clothing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothing
MM is the Military Medal, a British decoration

explanation.surface: A medal pinned onto a uniform as recognition of a great feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medal' looks like the subject being worn, but it is the abbreviation for the Military Medal, a British award, tucked into the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the peak, figuratively the highest point a person reaches.

clue.text: Jew has pride when abused

indicators.note: abused means misused or mistreated, so the letters of the words before it are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Jewish man shows his pride under ill-treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when abused' rearranges the eight letters of HAS PRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sephardi is a Jew of Spanish or Portuguese descent, an example of the wider term.

clue.text: At least car's quiet

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car; the 's links it to the next piece
mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that at least their car is a quiet one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At least' looks like an opening aside but is the definition: as a minimum.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'at the least' means the lowest acceptable amount, the smallest figure possible.

clue.text: One comes into something when another leaves

definitions.text: One comes into something when another leaves

parts.words: One comes into something when another leaves
parts.note: read as someone entering a room as another walks out, but 'comes into' means receives a legacy and 'leaves' means dies, or leaves property in a will

explanation.surface: A person enters just as another walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'come into' money is to inherit it, and someone 'leaves' it to you in their will when they die.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir receives property once its previous owner dies and bequeaths it.

clue.text: A call for help to install top-quality insulator

indicators.note: the distress call is to install the next piece, holding it within its letters

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
best means of the highest quality

explanation.surface: Someone phones for help to have first-rate insulation fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insulator' is the definition: the mineral fibre, not a material in general.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral fibre was widely used as heat and fire insulation before its health dangers were known.

clue.text: They're arranged to avoid liquidity problems when changing banks

definitions.text: They're arranged to avoid liquidity problems when changing banks

parts.words: They're arranged to avoid liquidity problems when changing banks
parts.note: read as a financial scheme for switching between banks, but the banks are river banks and liquidity is the water itself: a row of stones lets you cross without getting wet

explanation.surface: Measures put in place to stop cash-flow trouble while switching between lenders.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks are the two sides of a stream, and the 'liquidity problem' is getting your feet wet while crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: These are flat stones laid across a stream so a walker can cross from one bank to the other dry-shod.

clue.text: German scientist abandoning his first Alpine climb

indicators.note: the scientist abandons his own first letter, so his name loses its opening

parts.note: Hans Geiger was the German physicist behind the radiation counter

explanation.surface: A German researcher gives up on his first mountain ascent in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning his first' drops the G from GEIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss mountain, famous for its north face, is a classic and dangerous ascent for mountaineers.

clue.text: Working during dull interval in concert, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece comes during the other, so it sits within it

parts.note: trite means stale and unoriginal
on means operating or working, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: Performing through a tedious break in a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The concert interval sounds like a refreshment break, but it is a musical span of three whole tones.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory a span of three whole tones is a named interval heard in concert pieces among others.

clue.text: Angle not altogether covered in total religious practice

indicators.note: the trimmed piece is covered in the total, which wraps around it

parts.note: a sum is a total

indicators.note: not altogether means not completely, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: An angle partly covered in an overall total, in some religious exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle' is the verb, to go fishing, cut short by 'not altogether' before 'covered in' wraps the total round it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mystical tradition within Islam, a body of devotional belief and observance.

clue.text: Lively sort of bar at first keen to serve everyone

indicators.note: the bar type is placed at first, ahead of the other word

parts.note: the public bar is one room of a British pub
spirited means lively and energetic

explanation.surface: A lively pub's eager staff are ready to serve all customers.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'public bar' is the plainer room of a traditional British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Being civic-minded means caring for the community and wanting to help the common good.

clue.text: On top, flat or sloping roof

definitions.meaning: a luxury apartment on the top floor of a building
an old sense: a lean-to roof sloping from a wall

explanation.surface: Describing a building: is that roof flat or does it slope?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is older: a sloping shed roof attached to a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-floor apartment is the usual sense; a lean-to shelter is the original one.

clue.text: Composer curtailed loud emotion

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Edvard Grieg was the Norwegian composer of Peer Gynt
f is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A composer cut short a piece full of loud feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the last G from GRIEG, then F for forte follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sorrow is a strong feeling, especially after loss.

clue.text: Naval officer appearing in Butterfly

definitions.meaning: a commander of a fleet, the top rank in a navy
the red ... and white ... are butterflies

explanation.surface: A sailor of high rank turns up in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfly' suggests Puccini's opera Madama Butterfly, which has a naval officer in it, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet commander holds the senior rank; red admirals are common European butterflies.

clue.text: Dangerous room finally modified

indicators.note: the word's final letter is modified, swapped for a different one

parts.note: a parlour is a sitting room

explanation.surface: A room has been made unsafe by late alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally modified' changes the last R of PARLOUR to S.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous is an old form of perilous, meaning full of risk.

clue.text: Give up after half time

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half, as in demigod

explanation.surface: Throw in the towel once half-time comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: the definition gives up after the wordplay is applied.
explanation.definitionFit: To demit is to resign an office, to relinquish a position.

clue.text: Judge Tory party right

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A judge weighs whether the Tory party is in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political after Tory but means a side, as in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something is to weigh it up and think it over carefully.

clue.text: Offended about answer designed not to shock

indicators.note: the first word goes about the second, enclosing it

parts.note: insulted means offended

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence over a reply meant to avoid causing upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests upset feelings, but it is electric shock. 'about' puts A inside INSULTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiring wrapped in non-conducting material is protected from giving an electric shock.

clue.text: White for Pope

definitions.meaning: white symbolises purity, being free of guilt or sin

explanation.surface: White is the colour worn by the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Pope's white robes; each word is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: White stands for blamelessness, and several pontiffs bore this papal name.

clue.text: Having gone into alternative cost, sound happy about bribes

indicators.note: the reversed sound has gone into the rearranged word, so it sits inside it
an alternative form of the word is a new order of its letters
about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a cat purrs when it is happy

explanation.surface: Paying off officials: the happy sound when an alternative price gets through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges the letters of cost to COTS; 'about' turns the cat's sound backwards to RRUP, which 'Having gone into' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bribe someone is to pay them to act dishonestly, debasing their integrity.

clue.text: 20's former condition

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is': the entry at 20 across is this

parts.note: old means former, as in 'my old school'
nick means condition in British slang, as in 'in good nick'

explanation.surface: Asking what shape something at number 20 was in before.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer at 20 across, with 's meaning 'is'. 'In good nick' is British slang for in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: This old nickname refers to the Devil, the fallen angel.

clue.text: Angel once taking a temperature in nursing home

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes in the nursing home, placed inside it

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a convalescent home

explanation.surface: A former angel has their temperature taken in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and T inside SAN. 'Angel once' is fair because the Devil was an angel before his fall.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition the Devil was Lucifer, an angel who rebelled and was cast out of heaven.

clue.text: Implying one footballer's incompetent? Not hopeless for defence

definitions.meaning: a football side has eleven players, so saying '...' implies the remaining one is useless
able to be held or defended, as a position or argument is

explanation.surface: A remark that one player is useless, but the team is still decent at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: of a football team's eleven, 'ten able' leaves one who is not.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument or fort that can be held against attack is defensible.

clue.text: Easy task — having succeeded, sing heartily

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
to troll is an old verb meaning to sing in a full, jovial voice

explanation.surface: Having won, someone bursts into hearty song: it was simple.
explanation.walkthrough: TROLL here is an old verb: to sing a round loudly and merrily.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkover is an easy win, and so is a 'stroll' in sporting slang.

clue.text: Little fish beginning to take head off crustacean

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word means only its first letter is used
head off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the fiddler crab is a crustacean with one oversized claw

explanation.surface: A small fish takes the head off a crab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives T from 'take'; 'head off' removes F from FIDDLER, the fiddler crab.
explanation.definitionFit: British children call a minnow or stickleback by this name, any tiny fish.

clue.text: Asian country containing grand old capital

indicators.note: the country is containing the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An Asian nation with a fine former seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian country' points to the answer's region, but the capital is in Africa. 'containing' puts G inside LAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Nigerian city was the national seat of government until Abuja replaced it in 1991.

clue.text: English book holiday place in Florida

definitions.meaning: Virginia Woolf's novel, an English classic of 1928
the Florida city famed for its theme parks

explanation.surface: Reading an English novel on holiday in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: Woolf's novel follows a hero who lives for centuries and changes sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolf's novel shares its title with the resort city of Disney World.

clue.text: Down from duck — part of one

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
a wing is part of a duck

explanation.surface: Down feathers come from a duck, part of one at least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like feathers but means in debt. In cricket a batter out for nothing has made a 'duck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down by some money means it is still owed, a debt outstanding.

clue.text: Rate changed by board open to fixing

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: a table is a board, as in 'board and lodging'

explanation.surface: A tariff altered by the directors could still be rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' looks like rigging after rates and boards but means curing. 'changed' rearranges the first word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness that responds to medical care can be cured, or remedied.

clue.text: Superior, for example, has such an edge

definitions.text: Superior, for example, has such an edge

parts.words: Superior, for example, has such an edge
parts.note: reads as someone superior having an advantage, but Superior is the North American Great Lake and its edge is its shore

explanation.surface: Being superior gives you a certain advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like an adjective, but it is Lake Superior; 'edge' means shore, not advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore of a body of water is its edge, where the land begins.

clue.text: Prevent hidden diamonds coming to notice

indicators.note: the suit symbol is hidden within the other word, tucked inside it

parts.note: to avert is to prevent
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Stopping concealed gems from being noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' puts D inside AVERT. 'coming to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial is a public announcement promoting goods.
